title: The Fewest Buses From Stop to Stop

concept.title: Make the buses the nodes: one ride reaches every stop of a bus at once
body: Buses run in loops through some stops. You start at a stop `s` and may get on **any bus that serves it**; on a bus you can ride to any of its stops and change there to another bus. What is the smallest number of **buses** to reach the stop `t`? The first idea, a graph whose nodes are stops and whose edges join stops of the same bus, is far too big: a bus with 1000 stops would add half a million edges. Do not build it.

Look at the data as a **bipartite graph** with the stops on one side and the buses on the other, and an edge for every pair `(bus, stop)`. Now one ride is one step "stop -> bus" followed by "bus -> any of its stops". Run a BFS in **layers of rides**: the layer 0 is the stop `s`; to build the next layer, take every stop of the current layer, every bus not yet used that serves it, and every stop of that bus. Each bus is used **once** (the first time is the best), and so is each stop. The layer in which `t` appears is the number of buses.

Because every bus is expanded once, the total work is the number of pairs, O(n + r + m), however long the routes are. This is the standard way to handle "groups": when the nodes of a graph are joined in big cliques (all stops of one bus), add a **helper node** for the group instead of the edges. If the layers end without meeting `t`, the answer is -1.

statement: There are `n` bus stops and `r` buses; each bus serves a set of stops, given as `m` pairs `(bus, stop)`. You start at the stop `s` and can only move by bus: on a bus you may ride to any stop it serves, and at any stop you may change to any other bus that serves it. Print the smallest number of buses needed to get from `s` to `t` (0 if `s` equals `t`), or -1 if it is impossible.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`, `r` and `m`: the number of stops (numbered 1 to n), the number of buses (numbered 1 to r) and the number of pairs.
The second line has `s` and `t`: the stop where you start and the stop where you want to go.
Each of the next `m` lines has two numbers `b` and `x`: the bus `b` stops at the stop `x`.
outputFormat: Print the smallest number of buses, or -1.
constraints: The pairs are all different. A bus may serve any number of stops (also none), and a stop may be served by any number of buses (also none).

examples.note: The bus 1 serves the stops 1, 2, 7 and the bus 2 serves 3, 6, 7. Take the bus 1 from the stop 1 to the stop 7, then the bus 2 to the stop 6: 2 buses.

hints: Do not join the stops of a bus pairwise; think of the buses as extra nodes.
Process the search in layers; each layer is one more ride.
Take every bus only once, and every stop only once.

s, t = map(int, input().split())
pairs = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(m)]

explanation: A breadth-first search in layers of rides over the bipartite graph of stops and buses: every stop of the current layer boards every unused bus that serves it, and every stop of that bus joins the next layer. Each bus and each stop is handled once; the layer in which the target appears is the answer (0 if the start is the target, -1 if the layers run out).
solution.complexity: Time O(n + r + m), space O(n + r + m).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, r, m = map(int, input().split())
s, t = map(int, input().split())
pairs = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(m)]

buses_at = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
stops_of = [[] for _ in range(r + 1)]
for b, x in pairs:
    buses_at[x].append(b)
    stops_of[b].append(x)
answer = -1
if s == t:
    answer = 0
else:
    seen_bus = [False] * (r + 1)
    seen_stop = [False] * (n + 1)
    seen_stop[s] = True
    layer = [s]
    rides = 0
    while layer and answer < 0:
        rides += 1
        next_layer = []
        for x in layer:
            for b in buses_at[x]:
                if seen_bus[b]:
                    continue
                seen_bus[b] = True
                for y in stops_of[b]:
                    if y == t:
                        answer = rides
                    if not seen_stop[y]:
                        seen_stop[y] = True
                        next_layer.append(y)
        layer = next_layer
print(answer)
